Description

We want to integrate Google Analytics 4 (GA4) into the GoThru Dashboard. This will help our team better understand user navigation, popular features, and overall traffic to support data-driven product improvements.

Proposed Solution

  • Integrate Google Analytics 4 via a lightweight React integration (react-ga4).
  • Track page views automatically whenever a user navigates between dashboard routes.
  • Use environment variables to configure the Measurement ID so tracking can be easily managed across different environments (development vs production).

Scope of Work

  • Add Google Analytics 4 configuration using environment variables.
  • Initialize GA4 on application launch.
  • Track page views on route changes across the dashboard.
  • Ensure analytics gracefully disables if no Measurement ID is provided (e.g. in local development).

Acceptance Criteria

  • Navigating between pages triggers a page view event in the Google Analytics Realtime report.
  • Analytics setup does not affect dashboard load time or degrade user experience.
  • The application functions normally if the tracking ID is not configured.

Overview

Integrate Countly analytics tracking for the Global Action Receiver components in GoThru Dashboard (Layout.jsx and Level.jsx) that handle interactive RAG Copilot client signals (gothru:action).

This complements the widget-side tracking implemented in GoThruMedia/frontend-rag-system#60 by instrumenting the host dashboard execution phase. It isolates and categorizes all RAG action execution metrics using the standard rag_* namespace and segmentation metadata (feature: 'rag_copilot', source: 'dashboard_host') so that the complete conversion funnel from action offer -> trigger -> host execution can be analyzed in Countly without polluting core dashboard metrics.

Tracking Design & Event Schema

1. Event Namespace & Segmentation

All events must follow the rag_ prefix and include standardized categorization:

Event Name Trigger Condition Segmentation Properties
rag_client_action_executed Dashboard successfully executes a received gothru:action event (modal open, route navigation, file picker trigger) feature: "rag_copilot", source: "dashboard_host", action: string, target: string, status: "success"
rag_client_action_failed Dashboard fails to execute the action (e.g. target DOM element missing, invalid/unsupported action) feature: "rag_copilot", source: "dashboard_host", action: string, target: string, status: "failed", reason_code: string

2. Privacy & Safety Boundaries

  • Allowed: feature, source, action, target, status, reason_code.
  • Disallowed: No user tokens, auth headers, search queries, prompt texts, tour IDs / mid in raw strings (normalize route paths to patterns like /my-tours/:mid/upload), or arbitrary payload params.

Background

While a user's subscription is in dunning (past_due / unpaid after a failed renewal
payment), paid features are already gated via useDunningGate. However, the subscription
plan-change flows are not gated: a past-due user can still open the payment form to
upgrade/downgrade or buy a storage add-on, and only gets a raw backend error after submitting
(the backend rejects non-active subscriptions in getStripeSubscriptionDetail).

Goal

subscription is past due, and direct the user to settle the overdue payment first via the
existing global dunning modal ("Update Payment Method").

Scope

  • src/pages/Profile/Subscription/Subscription.jsx

    • handleBuySpaceAddon: space add-on "Buy Now"
  • src/components/organism/PaymentV2/Unsubscribe.jsx
    • handleDowngradeToBasic: "downgrade to BASIC" link inside the Unsubscribe modal

Out of Scope

  • Unsubscribing (cancel) remains allowed during dunning.
  • New subscriptions for pay-as-you-go users are not gated.
  • Backend guard / clearer API error message for upgrade, downgrade and space add-on (may be

    • Added secure rel="noopener noreferrer" attribute alongside standard target="_blank".
    • Browser now natively opens exactly 1 clean tab per click.
